items.name: Argumentative Writing — analytic rubric
items.summary: Five weighted criteria read across four bands. LSAC does not publish a numeric score for the writing section — admissions readers read the sample itself — so this rubric is a study instrument for diagnosing a draft, not a predictor of any official result.

bands.label: Developing
bands.descriptor: The reader can identify an attempt but has to supply the connective work themselves.

bands.label: Adequate
bands.descriptor: The moves are present but thin — asserted rather than argued, or handled unevenly across the response.

bands.label: Strong
bands.descriptor: The moves are present, deliberate, and carry their weight; a reader is persuaded even where they disagree.

bands.label: Exemplary
bands.descriptor: The response anticipates the reader's resistance and disarms it before it forms.

criteria.name: Position and thesis
criteria.description: Takes one defensible position on the stated issue and holds it. Readers should be able to state the writer's claim in a sentence after the first paragraph.
look_for: A thesis that names the position and the principal reason for it
A position that is actually contestable rather than a truism
The same position at the end as at the beginning

band_notes.1: The reader cannot tell which side the writer is on, or the position drifts mid-response.
band_notes.2: A position is stated but reads as a restatement of the prompt rather than a claim of the writer's own.
band_notes.3: A clear, contestable thesis with its principal reason attached, held throughout.
band_notes.4: A thesis precise enough to rule things out — the reader knows what evidence would refute it.

criteria.name: Reasoning and evidence
criteria.description: Supports the position with reasons that actually bear on it, and makes the connection between reason and claim explicit rather than leaving it to the reader.
look_for: Each supporting paragraph states a reason, not just a topic
The warrant linking reason to thesis is stated, not assumed
Claims are calibrated — hedged where the support is partial

band_notes.1: Assertions accumulate without support, or support is offered for a claim the thesis never made.
band_notes.2: Reasons are present but the link to the thesis is left implicit; the reader does the joining.
band_notes.3: Each reason is stated, supported, and explicitly tied back to the thesis.
band_notes.4: Reasoning is calibrated to its support — strong where the ground is firm, qualified where it is not.

criteria.name: Engagement with the given perspectives
criteria.description: Uses the perspectives supplied with the prompt as material to reason from, rather than restating them or ignoring them.
look_for: At least two of the supplied perspectives are engaged substantively
A perspective is interpreted or weighed, not merely quoted
A perspective that cuts against the position is not silently dropped

band_notes.1: The perspectives are ignored, or listed back without use.
band_notes.2: One perspective is used; the rest are decorative or absent.
band_notes.3: Several perspectives are weighed and put to work for the argument.
band_notes.4: A perspective that appears to cut against the position is reinterpreted so that it supports it, or is honestly conceded.

criteria.name: Counterargument and concession
criteria.description: States the strongest version of the opposing position and answers it, conceding what genuinely must be conceded.
look_for: The opposing position is stated in a form its holders would accept
The response answers the objection rather than repeating the thesis
Concessions are real and are bounded so they do not swallow the claim

band_notes.1: No opposing position appears, or it appears only as a caricature.
band_notes.2: An objection is named but answered by restating the thesis more loudly.
band_notes.3: The strongest objection is stated fairly and given a real answer.
band_notes.4: A genuine concession is made and then bounded, leaving the thesis standing on narrower but firmer ground.

criteria.name: Organization and written expression
criteria.description: Orders the argument so each paragraph earns its place, and writes clearly enough that the reasoning is never obscured by the prose.
look_for: A reader can predict what each paragraph will do from its first sentence
Transitions carry argumentative weight, not just sequence
Sentence-level clarity; errors do not impede meaning

band_notes.1: Order appears arbitrary, or errors force the reader to reread to recover the meaning.
band_notes.2: A recognizable structure with paragraphs that overlap or wander; occasional interference from errors.
band_notes.3: Purposeful structure and clean prose; the argument is easy to follow.
band_notes.4: Structure that is itself an argument — each paragraph placed where it does the most work.
